title: cmd/tk command tests fail under heavy machine load
description:
Seen once during this epic: TestApproveCommand, TestRejectCommand and TestUpdateVerdictFlag all failed with "expected approve exit 0, got 2" during a full go test ./... run, while a cloud run, two pollers and a stream of API fetches were saturating the machine. The same tree passed on origin/main alone, on the epic branch before the merge, on the single test in isolation, on the cmd/tk package alone, and on a full re-run once the machine was quiet.

Exit 2 rather than an assertion failure suggests the spawned binary was killed or timed out rather than misbehaving, so the likely cause is a deadline that is generous on an idle machine and not on a loaded one. Find the deadline and either make it robust or make the failure say "timed out" instead of reporting an exit code that reads like a usage error — the current message sent me looking for a merge regression that did not exist.

Do not fix this by lengthening a sleep. It matters because CI runners are loaded by definition, and this class already bit this repo once (the herdr AfterList ordering race in .tick/config.md).

2026-08-21 17:27 - CORRECTION to this tick's own hypothesis, and to the orchestrator's diagnosis. It was never a deadline and never load. These tests run IN-PROCESS, so nothing can be killed; exit 2 is exitUsage and was a genuine usage refusal. The three named tests share one path, resolveVerdictActor, which reads TK_ACTOR from the real process environment and refuses a runner-shaped actor. The orchestrator had exported TK_ACTOR=claude:orchestrator in its shell, go test inherited it, and the verdict guard refused for exactly the reason it exists. The load correlated because the thing saturating the machine WAS the run that exported the variable; every 'passed in isolation' re-run was typed in a shell without it. Verified after the fix: the suite now passes with TK_ACTOR set and unset.
closed_reason: Completed: command tests scrub the ambient tk environment instead of inheriting the operator's, so a shell that exports TK_ACTOR — which every agent run does — no longer makes the verdict guard refuse tests that never chose that actor. The reported cause (a load-sensitive deadline) was wrong twice over and the report records why.
